title: Desperately Seeking An Anchor
gist: Charles Gave and Louis-Vincent Gave argue a new monetary anchor is forming in Asia around the renminbi, while Western currencies and bond markets lose credibility as stores of value; because most of the world's excess savings are generated in Asia, that capital increasingly stays regional rather than funding US dollar, euro and Western bond assets.

insights.claim: A new monetary anchor is emerging in Asia, centered on the renminbi, at the same time that Western currencies and bond markets are becoming less reliable stores of value.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Argues for structural long exposure to renminbi-denominated and Asian assets and a lower strategic weight in Western sovereign bonds as the reserve-anchor role shifts.

themes.theme: Savings gravity and capital flow reversal

insights.claim: Most of the world's excess savings are generated in Asia, and more of that capital is expected to stay within the region rather than flow into Western assets.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Marginal buyers of Treasuries, bunds and Western credit shrink, implying wider term premia and a structurally weaker bid for Western duration.

insights.claim: Retained Asian savings are expected to erode the structural support underpinning the US dollar, the euro and Western bond markets.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Suggests a persistent, flow-driven headwind for DXY and EUR rather than a cyclical one; watch foreign participation in sovereign auctions as the confirming signal.
insights.locator: eroding structural support for the US dollar

insights.claim: The analysis is framed around the idea that the global system needs a monetary anchor, and that the location of that anchor — rather than short-term rate or growth differentials — is the variable that determines where capital ultimately settles.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Provides a lens for allocation: judge currencies and bonds by their credibility as stores of value, not by carry, when deciding long-horizon reserve-asset weights.
